sanskrit: etac chrutvāśrupūrṇākṣī parṇādasya viśāṃ pate damayantī raho 'bhyetya mātaraṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Hearing this, O lord of the people, Damayanti — her eyes filled with tears — went privately to her mother and addressed her thus.

sanskrit: ayam artho na saṃvedyo bhīme mātaḥ kathaṃ cana tvatsaṃnidhau samādekṣye sudevaṃ dvijasattamam
english: "This matter must not be known to Bhima in any way, mother. In your presence I shall send for Sudeva, that best of brahmins."

sanskrit: yathā na nṛpatir bhīmaḥ pratipadyeta me matam tathā tvayā prayattavyaṃ mama cet priyam icchasi
english: "You must take care that king Bhima does not come to know my intention, if you wish me well."

sanskrit: yathā cāhaṃ samānītā sudevenāśu bāndhavān tenaiva maṅgalenāśu sudevo yātu māciram samānetuṃ nalaṃ mātar ayodhyāṃ nagarīm itaḥ
english: "And as Sudeva quickly brought me back to my kinsmen by that same auspicious mission, so let Sudeva depart at once — do not delay, mother — to bring Nala here from the city of Ayodhyā."

sanskrit: viśrāntaṃ ca tataḥ paścāt parṇādaṃ dvijasattamam arcayām āsa vaidarbhī dhanenātīva bhāminī
english: Then, after he had rested, the beautiful Vaidarbhī honored Parṇāda, that best of brahmins, with great wealth.

sanskrit: nale cehāgate vipra bhūyo dāsyāmi te vasu tvayā hi me bahu kṛtaṃ yathā nānyaḥ kariṣyati yad bhartrāhaṃ sameṣyāmi śīghram eva dvijottama
english: "When Nala arrives here, O brahmin, I shall give you wealth again, for you have done me great service such as no other would do — that I shall be reunited swiftly with my husband, O foremost of the twice-born."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'rcayitvā tām āśīrvādaiḥ sumaṅgalaiḥ gṛhān upayayau cāpi kṛtārthaḥ sa mahāmanāḥ
english: Thus addressed, he honored her with most auspicious blessings and departed to his home, that high-minded one, his purpose fulfilled.

sanskrit: tataś cānāyya taṃ vipraṃ damayantī yudhiṣṭhira abravīt saṃnidhau mātur duḥkhaśokasamanvitā
english: Then Damayanti, O Yudhiṣṭhira, had that brahmin Sudeva summoned and, filled with grief and sorrow, spoke in her mother's presence.

sanskrit: gatvā sudeva nagarīm ayodhyāvāsinaṃ nṛpam ṛtuparṇaṃ vaco brūhi patim anyaṃ cikīrṣatī āsthāsyati punar bhaimī damayantī svayaṃvaram
english: "Go, Sudeva, to the city of Ayodhyā and speak to king Ṛtuparṇa these words: 'Wishing to take another husband, the daughter of Bhīma, Damayantī, will hold a svayaṃvara once more.'"

sanskrit: tatra gacchanti rājāno rājaputrāś ca sarvaśaḥ yathā ca gaṇitaḥ kālaḥ śvobhūte sa bhaviṣyati
english: "Kings and princes are all going there, and the time has been reckoned such that it shall take place tomorrow at sunrise."

sanskrit: yadi saṃbhāvanīyaṃ te gaccha śīghram ariṃdama sūryodaye dvitīyaṃ sā bhartāraṃ varayiṣyati na hi sa jñāyate vīro nalo jīvan mṛto 'pi vā
english: "If you think this worthy of consideration, go quickly, O subduer of enemies — at sunrise tomorrow she will choose a second husband, for that hero Nala is not known to be alive or dead."

sanskrit: evaṃ tayā yathoktaṃ vai gatvā rājānam abravīt ṛtuparṇaṃ mahārāja sudevo brāhmaṇas tadā
english: Exactly as she had instructed, Sudeva the brahmin went and spoke those words to king Ṛtuparṇa, O great king.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca śrutvā vacaḥ sudevasya ṛtuparṇo narādhipaḥ sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā vācā bāhukaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Hearing the words of Sudeva, king Ṛtuparṇa, lord of men, soothing him with gentle speech, addressed Bāhuka.

sanskrit: vidarbhān yātum icchāmi damadantyāḥ svayaṃvaram ekāhnā hayatattvajña manyase yadi bāhuka
english: "I wish to go to Vidarbha for Damayantī's svayaṃvara — in a single day, if you think it possible, O Bāhuka, who knows the truth about horses."

sanskrit: evam uktasya kaunteya tena rājñā nalasya ha vyadīryata mano duḥkhāt pradadhyau ca mahāmanāḥ
english: Hearing these words of the king, O Kaunteya, Nala's heart was torn with grief, and that high-minded one fell into deep reflection.

sanskrit: damayantī bhaved etat kuryād duḥkhena mohitā asmadarthe bhaved vāyam upāyaś cintito mahān
english: "Could this be Damayantī, bewildered by grief, doing this? Or could this be a great stratagem devised for my sake?"

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaṃ bata vaidarbhī kartukāmā tapasvinī mayā kṣudreṇa nikṛtā pāpenākṛtabuddhinā
english: "Alas, is the noble Vaidarbhī, that wretched woman, seeking to do something cruel, she who was abandoned by me — petty, sinful, of perverted judgment?"

sanskrit: strīsvabhāvaś calo loke mama doṣaś ca dāruṇaḥ syād evam api kuryāt sā vivaśā gatasauhṛdā mama śokena saṃvignā nairāśyāt tanumadhyamā
english: "The nature of women in the world is fickle, and my offense against her was severe — she might do this, being helpless, her affection gone, distressed by grief over me, that slender-waisted one, in despair."

sanskrit: na caivaṃ karhi cit kuryāt sāpatyā ca viśeṣataḥ yad atra tathyaṃ pathyaṃ ca gatvā vetsyāmi niścayam ṛtuparṇasya vai kāmam ātmārthaṃ ca karomy aham
english: "Yet she would never do this, especially as she has children. Whatever is true and right in this matter, I shall go and ascertain for certain. I shall fulfill Ṛtuparṇa's desire as well as my own purpose."

sanskrit: iti niścitya manasā bāhuko dīnamānasaḥ kṛtāñjalir uvācedam ṛtuparṇaṃ narādhipam
english: Having resolved thus in his mind, Bāhuka, though downcast in heart, folded his hands and spoke these words to Ṛtuparṇa, lord of men.

sanskrit: pratijānāmi te satyaṃ gamiṣyasi narādhipa ekāhnā puruṣavyāghra vidarbhanagarīṃ nṛpa
english: "I promise you truly, O lord of men, O tiger among men, O king — you shall reach the city of Vidarbha in a single day."

sanskrit: tataḥ parīkṣām aśvānāṃ cakre rājan sa bāhukaḥ aśvaśālām upāgamya bhāṅgasvarinṛpājñayā
english: Then, O king, Bāhuka went to the stables and, by the command of king Bhāṅgasvari, examined the horses.

sanskrit: sa tvaryamāṇo bahuśa ṛtuparṇena bāhukaḥ adhyagacchat kṛśān aśvān samarthān adhvani kṣamān
english: Though repeatedly urged by Ṛtuparṇa, Bāhuka selected lean horses that were capable and fit for the road.

sanskrit: tejobalasamāyuktān kulaśīlasamanvitān varjitāṃl lakṣaṇair hīnaiḥ pṛthuprothān mahāhanūn śuddhān daśabhir āvartaiḥ sindhujān vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: They were endowed with vigor and strength, of good breed and character, free from inferior marks, broad-nostriled and large-jawed, pure in ten whorls, born in Sindhu, swift as the wind.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tān abravīd rājā kiṃ cit kopasamanvitaḥ kim idaṃ prārthitaṃ kartuṃ pralabdhavyā hi te vayam
english: Seeing them, the king spoke with some irritation: "What is this? Is it your intention to deceive us with what you propose to do?"

sanskrit: katham alpabalaprāṇā vakṣyantīme hayā mama mahān adhvā ca turagair gantavyaḥ katham īdṛśaiḥ
english: "How shall these horses of mine, feeble in strength and vitality, carry me? The road is great, to be traveled by horses — how can it be done with such as these?"

sanskrit: bāhuka uvāca ete hayā gamiṣyanti vidarbhān nātra saṃśayaḥ athānyān manyase rājan brūhi kān yojayāmi te
english: Bāhuka said: "These horses will go to Vidarbha — there is no doubt in this. But if you think otherwise, O king, tell me which ones I should harness for you."

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇa uvāca tvam eva hayatattvajñaḥ kuśalaś cāsi bāhuka yān manyase samarthāṃs tvaṃ kṣipraṃ tān eva yojaya
english: Ṛtuparṇa said: "You alone know the truth about horses and are skilled in this, Bāhuka. Those which you judge capable, harness them quickly."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca tataḥ sadaśvāṃś caturaḥ kulaśīlasamanvitān yojayām āsa kuśalo javayuktān rathe naraḥ
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Then that skilled man harnessed four excellent horses of good breed and character, possessed of speed, to the chariot.

sanskrit: tato yuktaṃ rathaṃ rājā samārohat tvarānvitaḥ atha paryapatan bhūmau jānubhis te hayottamāḥ
english: Then the king mounted the harnessed chariot in great haste, but those best of horses sank to their knees on the ground.

sanskrit: tato naravaraḥ śrīmān nalo rājā viśāṃ pate sāntvayām āsa tān aśvāṃs tejobalasamanvitān
english: Then Nala, best of men, the splendid king, O lord of the people, pacified those horses endowed with vigor and strength.

sanskrit: raśmibhiś ca samudyamya nalo yātum iyeṣa saḥ sūtam āropya vārṣṇeyaṃ javam āsthāya vai param
english: And taking up the reins, Nala desired to set out, seating the charioteer Vārṣṇeya and adopting the highest speed.

sanskrit: te codyamānā vidhinā bāhukena hayottamāḥ samutpetur ivākāśaṃ rathinaṃ mohayann iva
english: Those best of horses, urged on properly by Bāhuka, leaped up as if into the sky, as if bewildering the chariot's passenger.

sanskrit: tathā tu dṛṣṭvā tān aśvān vahato vātaraṃhasaḥ ayodhyādhipatir dhīmān vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayau
english: Seeing those horses moving with the speed of the wind in that fashion, the wise lord of Ayodhyā was filled with the greatest amazement.

sanskrit: rathaghoṣaṃ tu taṃ śrutvā hayasaṃgrahaṇaṃ ca tat vārṣṇeyaś cintayām āsa bāhukasya hayajñatām
english: Hearing that thunder of the chariot and witnessing that mastery of the horses, Vārṣṇeya began to reflect on Bāhuka's knowledge of horses.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu syān mātalir ayaṃ devarājasya sārathiḥ tathā hi lakṣaṇaṃ vīre bāhuke dṛśyate mahat
english: "Can this be Mātali, the charioteer of the king of the gods? For such great marks are seen in the hero Bāhuka."

sanskrit: śālihotro 'tha kiṃ nu syād dhayānāṃ kulatattvavit mānuṣaṃ samanuprāpto vapuḥ paramaśobhanam
english: "Or could this be Śālihotra, who knows the true lineage of horses, having taken on a supremely beautiful human form?"

sanskrit: utāho svid bhaved rājā nalaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ so 'yaṃ nṛpatir āyāta ity evaṃ samacintayat
english: "Or could this be king Nala, the conqueror of enemy cities — is this the king arrived here?" Thus he reflected.

sanskrit: atha vā yāṃ nalo veda vidyāṃ tām eva bāhukaḥ tulyaṃ hi lakṣaye jñānaṃ bāhukasya nalasya ca
english: "Or else Bāhuka possesses the very knowledge that Nala knew, for I perceive the knowledge of Bāhuka and Nala to be equal."

sanskrit: api cedaṃ vayas tulyam asya manye nalasya ca nāyaṃ nalo mahāvīryas tadvidyas tu bhaviṣyati
english: "And even the age of this man I judge to be the same as Nala's — yet this is not Nala the great hero; still, he must be one who knows the same art."

sanskrit: pracchannā hi mahātmānaś caranti pṛthivīm imām daivena vidhinā yuktāḥ śāstroktaiś ca virūpaṇaiḥ
english: "For great-souled ones roam this earth in disguise, driven by the ordinance of fate and disfigured by means spoken of in the scriptures."

sanskrit: bhavet tu matibhedo me gātravairūpyatāṃ prati pramāṇāt parihīnas tu bhaved iti hi me matiḥ
english: "Yet my judgment wavers regarding the deformity of the body — that he is diminished in measure from his standard form is my conviction."

sanskrit: vayaḥpramāṇaṃ tattulyaṃ rūpeṇa tu viparyayaḥ nalaṃ sarvaguṇair yuktaṃ manye bāhukam antataḥ
english: "Age and stature are the same, but there is a difference in appearance; ultimately I think Bāhuka to be Nala, endowed with all virtues."

sanskrit: evaṃ vicārya bahuśo vārṣṇeyaḥ paryacintayat hṛdayena mahārāja puṇyaślokasya sārathiḥ
english: Thus deliberating again and again, Vārṣṇeya, the charioteer of the glorious Nala, reflected in his heart, O great king.

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇas tu rājendra bāhukasya hayajñatām cintayan mumude rājā sahavārṣṇeyasārathiḥ
english: But Ṛtuparṇa, O lord of kings, reflecting on Bāhuka's knowledge of horses, rejoiced, the king together with his charioteer Vārṣṇeya.

sanskrit: balaṃ vīryaṃ tathotsāhaṃ hayasaṃgrahaṇaṃ ca tat paraṃ yatnaṃ ca saṃprekṣya parāṃ mudam avāpa ha
english: Observing that strength, valor, and energy, that mastery of the horses, and that supreme effort, he attained the highest joy.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca sa nadīḥ parvatāṃś caiva vanāni ca sarāṃsi ca acireṇāticakrāma khecaraḥ khe carann iva
english: Bṛhadaśva said: He swiftly crossed rivers, mountains, forests, and lakes — like one moving through the sky, as if flying through the air.

sanskrit: tathā prayāte tu rathe tadā bhāṅgasvarir nṛpaḥ uttarīyam athāpaśyad bhraṣṭaṃ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: As the chariot moved on in this way, king Bhāṅgasvari, conqueror of enemy cities, saw his upper garment had fallen off.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tvaramāṇas tu paṭe nipatite tadā grahīṣyāmīti taṃ rājā nalam āha mahāmanāḥ
english: Then, as the cloth had fallen, the high-minded king said hastily to Nala: "I shall retrieve it."

sanskrit: nigṛhṇīṣva mahābuddhe hayān etān mahājavān vārṣṇeyo yāvad etaṃ me paṭam ānayatām iti
english: "Hold back these swift horses, O one of great intelligence, while Vārṣṇeya fetches this cloth for me."

sanskrit: nalas taṃ pratyuvācātha dūre bhraṣṭaḥ paṭas tava yojanaṃ samatikrānto na sa śakyas tvayā punaḥ
english: Nala replied to him: "Your cloth has fallen far away — we have gone past it by a yojana. It is not possible to retrieve it again."

sanskrit: evam ukte nalenātha tadā bhāṅgasvarir nṛpaḥ āsasāda vane rājan phalavantaṃ bibhītakam
english: When Nala had said this, O king, king Bhāṅgasvari then noticed a vibhītaka tree laden with fruit standing in the forest.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bāhukaṃ rājā tvaramāṇo 'bhyabhāṣata mamāpi sūta paśya tvaṃ saṃkhyāne paramaṃ balam
english: Seeing it, the king addressed Bāhuka in haste: "Look, charioteer, I too have supreme power in counting."

sanskrit: sarvaḥ sarvaṃ na jānāti sarvajño nāsti kaś cana naikatra pariniṣṭhāsti jñānasya puruṣe kva cit
english: "No one knows everything; there is no one who is omniscient. Knowledge does not reach its fullness in one place in any person anywhere."

sanskrit: vṛkṣe 'smin yāni parṇāni phalāny api ca bāhuka patitāni ca yāny atra tatraikam adhikaṃ śatam ekapatrādhikaṃ patraṃ phalam ekaṃ ca bāhuka
english: "On this tree, Bāhuka — the leaves and fruits, and those that have fallen here — one more than a hundred, one leaf more than that, and one fruit — [tell me the count], Bāhuka."

sanskrit: pañca koṭyo 'tha patrāṇāṃ dvayor api ca śākhayoḥ pracinuhy asya śākhe dve yāś cāpy anyāḥ praśākhikāḥ ābhyāṃ phalasahasre dve pañconaṃ śatam eva ca
english: "There are five crores of leaves on both of its two branches — cut these two branches of it with all their sub-branches; from these two there are two thousand fruits and ninety-five."

sanskrit: tato rathād avaplutya rājānaṃ bāhuko 'bravīt parokṣam iva me rājan katthase śatrukarśana
english: Then Bāhuka leaped down from the chariot and said to the king: "You are boasting of something beyond my sight, O king, O afflicteor of enemies."

sanskrit: atha te gaṇite rājan vidyate na parokṣatā pratyakṣaṃ te mahārāja gaṇayiṣye bibhītakam
english: "But if you have counted it, O king, it is not beyond sight — I shall count the vibhītaka before your eyes, O great king."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi nābhijānāmi bhaved evaṃ na veti ca saṃkhyāsyāmi phalāny asya paśyatas te janādhipa muhūrtam iva vārṣṇeyo raśmīn yacchatu vājinām
english: "I do not know whether it is so or not — I shall count the fruits of this before your watching eyes, O lord of men. Let Vārṣṇeya hold the reins of the horses for a moment."

sanskrit: tam abravīn nṛpaḥ sūtaṃ nāyaṃ kālo vilambitum bāhukas tv abravīd enaṃ paraṃ yatnaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: The king said to the charioteer: "This is no time to delay." But Bāhuka, exerting his utmost effort, addressed him.

sanskrit: pratīkṣasva muhūrtaṃ tvam atha vā tvarate bhavān eṣa yāti śivaḥ panthā yāhi vārṣṇeyasārathiḥ
english: "Wait a moment — or if you are in haste, this road leads safely onward; go with Vārṣṇeya as your charioteer."

sanskrit: abravīd ṛtuparṇas taṃ sāntvayan kurunandana tvam eva yantā nānyo 'sti pṛthivyām api bāhuka
english: Ṛtuparṇa said, pacifying him, O joy of the Kurus: "You alone are the driver — there is no other on earth, Bāhuka."

sanskrit: tvatkṛte yātum icchāmi vidarbhān hayakovida śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapanno 'smi na vighnaṃ kartum arhasi
english: "It is for your sake I wish to go to Vidarbha, O expert in horses — I have taken refuge in you; you ought not to create an obstacle."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ ca te kariṣyāmi yan māṃ vakṣyasi bāhuka vidarbhān yadi yātvādya sūryaṃ darśayitāsi me
english: "I shall fulfill your desire in whatever you tell me, Bāhuka, if you show me the sun while traveling to Vidarbha today."

sanskrit: athābravīd bāhukas taṃ saṃkhyāyemaṃ bibhītakam tato vidarbhān yāsyāmi kuruṣvedaṃ vaco mama
english: Then Bāhuka said to him: "After counting this vibhītaka I shall go to Vidarbha — do this at my word."

sanskrit: akāma iva taṃ rājā gaṇayasvety uvāca ha so 'vatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ śātayām āsa taṃ drumam
english: The king said as if unwillingly: "Count then." He quickly descended from the chariot and felled that tree.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo rājānam idam abravīt gaṇayitvā yathoktāni tāvanty eva phalāni ca
english: Then, filled with wonder, after counting — there were exactly as many fruits as had been said — he spoke these words to the king.

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ rājan dṛṣṭavān asmi te balam śrotum icchāmi tāṃ vidyāṃ yathaitaj jñāyate nṛpa
english: "This is truly extraordinary, O king — I have witnessed your power. I wish to hear of that knowledge by which this is known, O king."

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rājā tvarito gamane tadā viddhy akṣahṛdayajñaṃ māṃ saṃkhyāne ca viśāradam
english: Then the king, eager to proceed on his way, said to him: "Know me to be one who knows the heart of dice and is expert in calculation."

sanskrit: bāhukas tam uvācātha dehi vidyām imāṃ mama matto 'pi cāśvahṛdayaṃ gṛhāṇa puruṣarṣabha
english: Then Bāhuka said to him: "Give me this knowledge, and receive from me in return the heart of horses, O bull among men."

sanskrit: ṛtuparṇas tato rājā bāhukaṃ kāryagauravāt hayajñānasya lobhāc ca tathety evābravīd vacaḥ
english: Then king Ṛtuparṇa, out of the importance of his purpose and out of desire for knowledge of horses, said to Bāhuka: "So be it."

sanskrit: yatheṣṭaṃ tvaṃ gṛhāṇedam akṣāṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ param nikṣepo me 'śvahṛdayaṃ tvayi tiṣṭhatu bāhuka evam uktvā dadau vidyām ṛtuparṇo nalāya vai
english: "Take as you wish this supreme heart of dice; let my horse-knowledge remain deposited with you, Bāhuka." Having spoken thus, Ṛtuparṇa gave the knowledge to Nala.

sanskrit: tasyākṣahṛdayajñasya śarīrān niḥsṛtaḥ kaliḥ karkoṭakaviṣaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ mukhāt satatam udvaman
english: From the body of that knower of the heart of dice, Kali emerged, constantly vomiting from his mouth the sharp poison of Karkoṭaka.

sanskrit: kales tasya tadārtasya śāpāgniḥ sa viniḥsṛtaḥ sa tena karśito rājā dīrghakālam anātmavān
english: From that afflicted Kali went forth the fire of a curse. By him the king had been tormented for a long time, without self-mastery.

sanskrit: tato viṣavimuktātmā svarūpam akarot kaliḥ taṃ śaptum aicchat kupito niṣadhādhipatir nalaḥ
english: Then Kali, freed from the poison, assumed his own form. The enraged lord of Niṣadha, Nala, desired to curse him.

sanskrit: tam uvāca kalir bhīto vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ kopaṃ saṃyaccha nṛpate kīrtiṃ dāsyāmi te parām
english: Kali, trembling with fear and with folded hands, said to him: "Restrain your anger, O king — I shall give you the highest fame."

sanskrit: indrasenasya jananī kupitā māśapat purā yadā tvayā parityaktā tato 'haṃ bhṛśapīḍitaḥ
english: "Formerly the mother of Indrasena, enraged, cursed me when she was abandoned by you — from that time I was greatly tormented."

sanskrit: avasaṃ tvayi rājendra suduḥkham aparājita viṣeṇa nāgarājasya dahyamāno divāniśam
english: "I dwelt within you, O unconquered lord of kings, in the greatest misery, burning day and night with the poison of the serpent king."

sanskrit: ye ca tvāṃ manujā loke kīrtayiṣyanty atandritāḥ matprasūtaṃ bhayaṃ teṣāṃ na kadā cid bhaviṣyati
english: "And those men in the world who shall celebrate you without ceasing — fear arising from me shall never come to them."

sanskrit: evam ukto nalo rājā nyayacchat kopam ātmanaḥ tato bhītaḥ kaliḥ kṣipraṃ praviveśa bibhītakam kalis tv anyena nādṛśyat kathayan naiṣadhena vai
english: Thus addressed, king Nala restrained his anger. Then Kali, frightened, quickly entered into the vibhītaka tree; and Kali was not seen by others, as he conversed thus with the Niṣadhan.
